result.topic_en: Mixed calculations: a faint variational/differential computation with sums over p_i and sigma; remarks on functions whose values jump at points x = p/2n and on one-sided limits f(x+0), f(x-0) for functions without infinitely many maxima and minima; an asymptotic (stationary-phase type) evaluation of integrals ∫F(x)cos(f(x) − nx)dx giving powers of α; and a solution of x log x = log a by iterated logarithms.

Stationary point condition for the phase of the oscillatory integral
Quadratic (Taylor) expansion of the phase about the stationary point
Change of variable dx in terms of dy near the stationary point

Solution of x log x = log a by iterated logarithms
One-sided limits equal to the function value away from the points x = p/2n

[Stetig-] {+Stetig+} ist der [-...-] {+Werth+} von [-f(x)-] [?] obwohl wenn der Argumentwerth abnehmend {+stetig+} oder wenn er zunehmend gleich x wird, sprungweise [?] einen festen Grenzwerth, und zwar ist,

items.english: The value of f(x) is continuous, although when the argument becomes equal to x decreasing (continuously) or increasing, it [approaches] a fixed limit value by a jump, namely when x = p/2n (where p, n are relatively prime); elsewhere, however, everywhere f(x+0) = f(x), f(x−0) = f(x).

items.quote: Es ist nicht schwer zu beweisen, dass der Werth einer Function [-f(x)-] welche nicht unendlich viele Maxima u. Minima hat, [-...-] stets, sowohl wenn der Argumentwerth abnehmend als wenn er zunehmend = x wird, {+entweder+} festen Grenzwerthen f(x+0) u. f(x-0) sich nähern [-müsste-], oder unendlich groß werden müsste.
items.english: It is not hard to prove that the value of a function which does not have infinitely many maxima and minima must always, whether the argument becomes equal to x decreasing or increasing, either approach fixed limit values f(x+0) and f(x−0), or become infinitely large.
